title: Fake News on Social Media
text:
Many people read news on social media every day. Some posts are true, but others are fake news. Fake news is a story that is not real, but it looks like real news. People often share stories quickly, without checking them first.

Before you share a post, you should check the facts. Look at the website and read more than the title. If a story makes you very angry or very scared, stop and think. Ask a friend or a teacher if you are not sure.

options: A story that is not real but looks like real news

questions.text: What should you do before you share a post?
options: Send it to everyone at once

questions.text: Why might a story that makes you very angry be a reason to stop and think?
options: Strong feelings can make people share stories without checking them
Angry stories are always written by teachers
Stories that make people angry are always funny

questions.text: What does the writer probably think about sharing posts quickly?
options: It is the best way to learn the news
It makes every story become true

vocabulary.definition: not real, made to look like something true
to send a post or story to other people
information that is known to be true

paragraph_translations: Birçok insan her gün sosyal medyada haber okur. Bazı paylaşımlar doğrudur, ama diğerleri sahte haberdir. Sahte haber gerçek olmayan, ama gerçek haber gibi görünen bir hikâyedir. İnsanlar hikâyeleri genellikle önce kontrol etmeden hızlıca paylaşır.

Bir paylaşımı göndermeden önce gerçekleri kontrol etmelisiniz. Web sitesine bakın ve sadece başlığı değil, daha fazlasını okuyun. Bir hikâye sizi çok kızdırır ya da çok korkutursa durup düşünün. Emin değilseniz bir arkadaşınıza veya öğretmeninize sorun.
